title: K-Fire (K-火): Network-Aware Utility-Pole Fire Risk
role: Presenter & Team Member · Team ASIAN UNION
one_liner: Grand Prize · 2026 Weather Big Data Contest, Disaster Safety
problem: How can 1.39 million utility poles in Gangwon be prioritized for inspection when true grid connections and labeled fire-risk data are unavailable?
approach: Reconstructed an approximate power-grid graph from pole geometry and public transmission data, then combined network structure with wildfire, weather, forest, terrain, and accessibility features in an interpretable frequency-ratio and Random Forest ensemble.
why_it_matters: The highest-risk 20% captured 46% of held-out wildfires—2.3× random—with an AUC of 0.728, supporting targeted inspections, vegetation management, and grid reinforcement.

title: AI Weather Quest 2025
one_liner: ECMWF's global sub-seasonal forecasting competition (days 19–32, 1.5° resolution, probabilistic).
problem: Sub-seasonal forecasting (days 19–32) is the 'predictability desert' between weather and climate. Can data-driven post-processing make ECMWF's ensemble skillful and calibrated?
approach: Designed a geo-aware 3D U-Net and integrated the van Leeuwen et al. (2025) 4-source Bayesian uncertainty framework, turning deterministic post-processing into calibrated quintile-probability forecasts.
why_it_matters: Led a 4-person team submitting weekly forecasts across the competition periods; accepted for presentation at S2S2D 2026 (Reading, UK).
